Placemaker.Settings.ApplyParkStats.Desc: Parks and plazas you build add their attractiveness to the city's tourism, like vanilla parks. Turning it off removes it from existing builds on the next load.
Placemaker.ParkStats.F.Size: Size {0} m² gives a base of {1} (1.9 × (area ÷ 1,000 m²)^0.85, fitted to vanilla parks).
Placemaker.ParkStats.F.Quality: Quality ×{0} = 0.55 + trees {1} + water {2} + landmarks {3} + amenities {4} + play and sport {5} + seating {6}.
Placemaker.ParkStats.F.Band: Vanilla parks of a similar size, scaled to this size: {0} to {1}.
Placemaker.ParkStats.F.AttrGame: In game it is multiplied by the terrain bonus (forest, shore, height: up to +40 %) when built. The city adds every park's attractiveness² ÷ 10,000 into its tourism.
Placemaker.ParkStats.F.LeisureGame: Vanilla parks: each visit raises a citizen's leisure by about this ÷ 5 per update until they are satisfied.
Placemaker.ParkStats.F.CoverageGame: Vanilla parks: coverage fades with walking distance as 1 − (distance ÷ range)², times the entertainment strength.
Placemaker.ParkStats.F.CapacityGame: Vanilla parks: each covered street uses up capacity by its length and density; when it runs out, coverage fades.
Placemaker.ParkStats.F.EntertainmentGame: Vanilla parks: residents get up to 20 wellbeing from park coverage (20 × √(coverage ÷ 1.5), at most 20).
Placemaker.ParkStats.F.UpkeepGame: What a vanilla park this good costs to run (about a fifth of its price per month).
